drafted_from: tool row in tools/start-a-computer/tool-rows.json, do-work/start-a-computer.mjs (installOnPlace) and tools/start-a-computer/test/start-a-computer.test.mjs
start_here: Say to your AI: "Put engine release r2, already built at /opt/build/release on my computer arm1, live on it and restart it."
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it reads a lease file and a request file and changes the release on one machine.
instructions: 1. Have the lease file (lease.json) and write request.json with ssh {known_hosts}, engine {file, release_name, release {on_machine} or {tarball}} and name {host_name}.

2. Say the line in start_here. Your AI reads the row with tools:list {tool: "tool:give-a-computer-a-new-release"} and runs node tools/start-a-computer/do-work/start-a-computer.mjs install lease.json request.json. No credential is needed; it reaches the machine over SSH.
3. Read {release, sign_up_status}. The old release stays beside the new one: going back is the same command with the old release_name.

worked_examples.title: Release r2 copied beside the old ones, the service restarted, the page read
worked_examples.ask: Switch my computer to release r2.
worked_examples.given: From tools/start-a-computer/test/start-a-computer.test.mjs ('an install on a running place is judged by its health row...'). lease.json = {"schema":"place-lease/1","provider":"existing-machine","name":"arm1","address":"192.0.2.9","adopted":true,"hostName":"place.example.com"}; request.json = {"ssh":{"known_hosts":"known_hosts"},"engine":{"file":"trillion-local","release_name":"r2","release":{"on_machine":"/opt/build/release"}},"name":{"host_name":"place.example.com"}}; the config on the machine says listen 127.0.0.1:7199 and https://place.example.com/readyz answers 200. Run: node tools/start-a-computer/do-work/start-a-computer.mjs install lease.json request.json
worked_examples.hands_back: {"release":"/opt/place/releases/r2","sign_up_status":200}: /opt/place/releases/r2 was copied from /opt/build/release, /opt/place/releases/current now points at it, place.service was restarted and the public /readyz page answered 200.
